2473510.name: Greater Prairie-Chicken
2473510.blurb: The greater prairie-chicken or pinnated grouse (Tympanuchus cupido), sometimes called a boomer, is a large bird in the grouse tribe.

2473958.name: Gray Partridge
2473958.blurb: The grey partridge (Perdix perdix) is a bird in the pheasant family Phasianidae of the order Galliformes, gallinaceous birds. The scientific name is the Latin for "partridge".

2474337.name: Limpkin
2474337.blurb: The limpkin (Aramus guarauna), also called carrao, courlan, and crying bird, is a large wading bird related to rails and cranes, and the only extant species in the family Aramidae.

2474393.name: American Coot
2474393.blurb: The American coot (Fulica americana), also known as a mud hen or pouldeau, is a bird of the family Rallidae. Though commonly mistaken for ducks, American coots are only distantly related to ducks, belonging to a separate order.

2474639.name: Sora
2474639.blurb: The sora, sora rail or Carolina crake (Porzana carolina) is a small waterbird of the rail family Rallidae, sometimes also referred to as the sora rail or sora crake, that occurs throughout much of North America.

2474825.name: Virginia Rail
2474825.blurb: The Virginia rail (Rallus limicola) is a small waterbird, of the family Rallidae. These birds remain fairly common despite continuing loss of habitat, but are secretive by nature and more often heard than seen.

2474953.name: Sandhill Crane
2474953.blurb: The sandhill crane (Antigone canadensis) is a species of large crane of North America and extreme northeastern Siberia.

2475472.name: Belted Kingfisher
2475472.blurb: The belted kingfisher (Megaceryle alcyon) is a large, conspicuous water kingfisher, native to North America.

2478106.name: Red-bellied Woodpecker
2478106.blurb: The red-bellied woodpecker (Melanerpes carolinus) is a medium-sized woodpecker of the family Picidae. It breeds mainly in the eastern United States, ranging as far south as Florida and as far north as Canada.

2478130.name: Red-headed Woodpecker
2478130.blurb: The red-headed woodpecker (Melanerpes erythrocephalus) is a mid-sized woodpecker found in temperate North America. Its breeding habitat is open country across southern Canada and the east-central United States.

2478259.name: Northern Flicker
2478259.blurb: The northern flicker or common flicker (Colaptes auratus) is a medium-sized bird of the woodpecker family. It is native to most of North America, parts of Central America, Cuba, and the Cayman Islands,

2478605.name: Yellow-bellied Sapsucker
2478605.blurb: The yellow-bellied sapsucker (Sphyrapicus varius) is a medium-sized woodpecker that breeds in Canada and the northeastern United States.

2480295.name: Semipalmated Plover
2480295.blurb: The semipalmated plover (Charadrius semipalmatus) is a small plover. Charadrius is a Late Latin word for a yellowish bird mentioned in the fourth-century Vulgate.

2480320.name: Killdeer
2480320.blurb: The killdeer (Charadrius vociferus) is a large plover found in the Americas. Its shrill, two-syllable call is often heard, sounding like "kill deer".

2480327.name: Black-bellied Plover
2480327.blurb: The grey plover or black-bellied plover (Pluvialis squatarola) is a large plover breeding in Arctic regions. It is a long-distance migrant, with a nearly worldwide coastal distribution when not breeding.

2480446.name: Bald Eagle
2480446.blurb: The bald eagle (Haliaeetus leucocephalus) is a bird of prey found in North America. A sea eagle, it has two known subspecies and forms a species pair with the white-tailed eagle (Haliaeetus albicilla),

2480487.name: Hen Harrier
2480487.blurb: The hen harrier (Circus cyaneus) is a bird of prey. It breeds in open areas such as marshes and grasslands in Eurasia and is migratory, moving further south outside of the breeding season.

2480506.name: Golden Eagle
2480506.blurb: The golden eagle (Aquila chrysaetos) is a bird of prey living in the Northern Hemisphere. It is the most widely distributed species of eagle. Like all eagles, it belongs to the family Accipitridae.

2480524.name: Rough-legged Hawk
2480524.blurb: The rough-legged buzzard (Europe) or rough-legged hawk (North America) (Buteo lagopus) is a medium-large bird of prey.

2480529.name: Red-shouldered Hawk
2480529.blurb: The red-shouldered hawk (Buteo lineatus) is a medium-sized buteo. Its breeding range spans eastern North America, along the coast of California and northern to northeastern-central Mexico.

2480538.name: Broad-winged Hawk
2480538.blurb: The broad-winged hawk (Buteo platypterus) is a medium-sized hawk of the genus Buteo. During the summer, some subspecies are distributed over eastern North America, as far west as British Columbia and Texas;

2480542.name: Red-tailed Hawk
2480542.blurb: The red-tailed hawk (Buteo jamaicensis) is a bird of prey and one of the most common hawks in North America. In the United States, it is one of three species colloquially known as the "chickenhawk".

2480562.name: Swainson's Hawk
2480562.blurb: Swainson's hawk (Buteo swainsoni) is a large bird species in the Accipitriformes order. This species was named after William Swainson, a British naturalist.

2480566.name: Ferruginous Hawk
2480566.blurb: The ferruginous hawk (Buteo regalis) is a large bird of prey and belongs to the broad-winged buteo hawks. An old colloquial name is ferrugineous rough-leg, due to its similarity to the closely related rough-legged hawk (B.

2480719.name: Mississippi Kite
2480719.blurb: The Mississippi kite (Ictinia mississippiensis) is a small bird of prey in the family Accipitridae. Mississippi kites have narrow, pointed wings and are graceful in flight, often appearing to float in the air.

2480726.name: Osprey
2480726.blurb: The osprey (; Pandion haliaetus), historically known as sea hawk, river hawk, and fish hawk, is a diurnal, fish-eating bird of prey with a cosmopolitan range.

2480863.name: Black-crowned Night Heron
2480863.blurb: The black-crowned night heron (Nycticorax nycticorax) or black-capped night heron, commonly shortened to just night heron in Eurasia, is a medium-sized heron found throughout a large part of the world, including parts of Europe,

2480881.name: Tricolored Heron
2480881.blurb: The tricolored heron (Egretta tricolor), formerly known as the Louisiana heron, is a small species of heron native to coastal parts of the Americas.

2480894.name: Little Blue Heron

audio.by: Mauricio Álvarez Rebolledo (Colección de Sonidos Ambientales - Instituto Humboldt)

2480894.blurb: The little blue heron (Egretta caerulea) is a small heron of the genus Egretta. It is a small, darkly colored heron with a two-toned bill. Juveniles are entirely white, bearing resemblance to the snowy egret.

2480953.name: Yellow-crowned Night Heron
2480953.blurb: The yellow-crowned night heron (Nyctanassa violacea) is one of two species of night heron in the genus Nyctanassa. Unlike the black-crowned night heron, which has a worldwide distribution,

2481000.name: Prairie Falcon
2481000.blurb: The prairie falcon (Falco mexicanus) is a medium-sized falcon found in Western North America. A separate species from the peregrine falcon, with which it shares some visual similarities, the prairie falcon is, essentially,

2481047.name: Peregrine Falcon
2481047.blurb: The peregrine falcon (Falco peregrinus), also referred to simply as the peregrine, is a bird of prey (raptor) in the family Falconidae known for its speed.

2481119.name: Black Tern
2481119.blurb: The black tern (Chlidonias niger) is a small tern generally found in or near inland water that breeds in Europe, Western Asia and North America. In winter the birds migrate to coastal areas of Africa and South America.

2481127.name: Glaucous Gull
2481127.blurb: The glaucous gull (Larus hyperboreus) is a large gull, the second-largest gull in the world. The genus name is from Latin larus, which appears to have referred to a gull or other large seabird.

2481134.name: Ring-billed Gull
2481134.blurb: The ring-billed gull (Larus delawarensis) is a medium-sized gull native to North America, breeding in Canada and the northern Contiguous United States, and wintering mainly in the United States and northern Mexico.

2481156.name: Iceland Gull
2481156.blurb: The Iceland gull (Larus glaucoides) is a medium-sized gull that breeds in the Arctic regions of Canada and Greenland, but not in Iceland (as its name suggests), where it is only seen during winter.

2481174.name: Lesser Black-backed Gull
2481174.blurb: The lesser black-backed gull (Larus fuscus) is a large gull that breeds on the Atlantic and Arctic coasts of Europe. It is migratory, wintering from the British Isles south to West Africa.

2481218.name: Ross's Gull
2481218.blurb: Ross's gull (Rhodostethia rosea) is a small gull, the only species in its genus, although it has been suggested the genus should be merged with the closely related Hydrocoloeus, which otherwise only includes the little gull.

2481236.name: Caspian Tern
2481236.blurb: The Caspian tern (Hydroprogne caspia) is the world's largest species of tern, with a subcosmopolitan but scattered distribution. Despite its extensive range, it is monotypic of its genus, and has no accepted subspecies.

2481670.name: Long-billed Dowitcher
2481670.blurb: The long-billed dowitcher (Limnodromus scolopaceus) is a medium-sized shorebird with a relatively long bill belonging to the sandpiper family, Scolopacidae.

2481680.name: Hudsonian Godwit
2481680.blurb: The Hudsonian godwit (Limosa haemastica) is a large shorebird in the sandpiper family, Scolopacidae. It is a long distance migratory species that breeds at remote sites in northern Canada and winters in southern South America.

2481705.name: Upland Sandpiper
2481705.blurb: The upland sandpiper (Bartramia longicauda) is a large sandpiper, closely related to the curlews. Older names are the upland plover and Bartram's sandpiper. In Louisiana, it is also colloquially known as the papabotte.

2481710.name: Solitary Sandpiper
2481710.blurb: The solitary sandpiper (Tringa solitaria) is a small shorebird. The genus name Tringa is the Neo-Latin name given to the green sandpiper by Aldrovandus in 1599 based on Ancient Greek trungas, a thrush-sized, white-rumped,

2481720.name: Greater Yellowlegs
2481720.blurb: The greater yellowlegs (Tringa melanoleuca) is a large shorebird in the family Scolopacidae. It breeds in central Canada and southern Alaska and winters in southern North America, Central America,

2481721.name: Lesser Yellowlegs
2481721.blurb: The lesser yellowlegs (Tringa flavipes) is a medium-sized shorebird. It breeds in the boreal forest region of North America.

2481744.name: Pectoral Sandpiper
2481744.blurb: The pectoral sandpiper (Calidris melanotos), often abbreviated pec, is a small, migratory wader that breeds in arctic regions of North America and Asia, wintering in South America and Oceania. It eats small invertebrates.

2481745.name: Least Sandpiper
2481745.blurb: The least sandpiper (Calidris minutilla) is the smallest shorebird. The genus name is from Ancient Greek kalidris or skalidris, a term used by Aristotle for some grey-coloured waterside birds.

2481759.name: Dunlin
2481759.blurb: The dunlin (Calidris alpina) is a small wader in the genus Calidris. The English name is a dialect form of "dunling", first recorded in 1531–1532.

2481764.name: Semipalmated Sandpiper
2481764.blurb: The semipalmated sandpiper (Calidris pusilla) is a very small shorebird. The genus name is from Ancient Greek kalidris or skalidris, a term used by Aristotle for some grey-coloured waterside birds.

2481770.name: Baird's Sandpiper
2481770.blurb: Baird's sandpiper (Calidris bairdii) is a small shorebird. It is among those Calidris species which were formerly sometimes included in the genus Erolia, which was subsumed into the genus Calidris in 1973.

2481798.name: Spotted Sandpiper
2481798.blurb: The spotted sandpiper (Actitis macularius) is a small shorebird. Together with its sister species the common sandpiper (A. hypoleucos), it makes up the genus Actitis.

2481817.name: Wilson's Snipe
2481817.blurb: Wilson's snipe (Gallinago delicata) is a small, stocky shorebird. The generic name Gallinago is Neo-Latin for a woodcock or snipe from Latin gallina, "hen" and the suffix -ago, "resembling".

2481930.name: Turkey Vulture
2481930.blurb: The turkey vulture (Cathartes aura) is the most widespread of the New World vultures. One of three species in the genus Cathartes of the family Cathartidae,

2481937.name: Wood Stork
2481937.blurb: The wood stork (Mycteria americana) is a large wading bird in the family Ciconiidae (storks). Originally described in 1758 by Carl Linnaeus,

2481957.name: Yellow-billed Loon

photo.by:
Ryan Askren

USGS, Alaska Science Center

2481957.blurb: The yellow-billed loon (Gavia adamsii), also known as the white-billed diver, is the largest member of the loon or diver family. Breeding adults have a black head, white underparts and a chequered black-and-white mantle.

2481962.name: Common Loon
2481962.blurb: The common loon or great northern diver (Gavia immer) is a large member of the loon, or diver, family of birds. Breeding adults have a plumage that includes a broad black head and neck with a greenish, purplish, or bluish sheen,

2482033.name: Western Grebe
2482033.blurb: The western grebe (Aechmophorus occidentalis) is a species in the grebe family of water birds. Folk names include "dabchick", "swan grebe" and "swan-necked grebe".

2482059.name: Horned Grebe
2482059.blurb: The horned grebe or Slavonian grebe (Podiceps auritus) is a relatively small and threatened species of waterbird in the family Podicipedidae. There are two subspecies, P. a.

2482077.name: Pied-billed Grebe
2482077.blurb: The pied-billed grebe (Podilymbus podiceps) is a species of the grebe family of water birds primarily found in ponds throughout the Americas.

2482507.name: American Crow
2482507.blurb: The American crow (Corvus brachyrhynchos) is a large passerine bird species of the family Corvidae. It is a common bird found throughout much of North America, only absent from the tundra biome.

2482593.name: Blue Jay
2482593.blurb: The blue jay (Cyanocitta cristata) is a passerine bird in the family Corvidae, native to eastern North America. It lives in most of the eastern and central United States; some eastern populations may be migratory.

2482785.name: Yellow-bellied Flycatcher
2482785.blurb: The yellow-bellied flycatcher (Empidonax flaviventris) is a small insect-eating bird of the tyrant flycatcher family.

2482786.name: Willow Flycatcher
2482786.blurb: The willow flycatcher (Empidonax traillii) is a small insect-eating, migrant bird of the tyrant flycatcher family native to North America.

2482791.name: Least Flycatcher
2482791.blurb: The least flycatcher (Empidonax minimus) (also called chebec, or chebecker, after the sound it makes) is a small insect-eating bird. It is the smallest Empidonax flycatcher in eastern North America.

2482802.name: Acadian Flycatcher
2482802.blurb: The Acadian flycatcher (Empidonax virescens) is a small insect-eating bird of the tyrant flycatcher family.

2482809.name: Alder Flycatcher
2482809.blurb: The alder flycatcher (Empidonax alnorum) is a small insect-eating bird in the tyrant flycatcher family. The genus name Empidonax is from Ancient Greek empis, "gnat", and anax, "master".

2483597.name: Great Crested Flycatcher
2483597.blurb: The great crested flycatcher (Myiarchus crinitus) is a large insect-eating bird of the tyrant flycatcher family. It is the most widespread member of the genus Myiarchus in North America,

2483606.name: Eastern Phoebe
2483606.blurb: The eastern phoebe (Sayornis phoebe) is a small passerine bird. The genus name Sayornis is constructed from the specific part of Charles Lucien Bonaparte's name for Say's phoebe, Muscicapa saya, and Ancient Greek ornis, "bird".

2484155.name: Common Grackle
2484155.blurb: The common grackle (Quiscalus quiscula) is an icterid bird found in large numbers through much of North America. It was first described in 1758 by Carl Linnaeus and has three officially recognized subspecies.

2484183.name: Brewer's Blackbird
2484183.blurb: Brewer's blackbird (Euphagus cyanocephalus) is a medium-sized New World blackbird. It is named after the ornithologist Thomas Mayo Brewer.

2484184.name: Rusty Blackbird
2484184.blurb: The rusty blackbird (Euphagus carolinus) is a medium-sized New World blackbird, closely related to grackles ("rusty grackle" is an older name for the species).

2484195.name: Yellow-headed Blackbird
2484195.blurb: The yellow-headed blackbird (Xanthocephalus xanthocephalus) is a medium-sized blackbird with a yellow head. It is the only member of the genus Xanthocephalus.

2484254.name: Eastern Meadowlark
2484254.blurb: The eastern meadowlark (Sturnella magna) is a medium-sized icterid bird, very similar in appearance to its sister species, the western meadowlark.

2484340.name: Baltimore Oriole
2484340.blurb: The Baltimore oriole (Icterus galbula) is a small icterid blackbird common in eastern North America as a migratory breeding bird.

2484391.name: Brown-headed Cowbird
2484391.blurb: The brown-headed cowbird (Molothrus ater) is a small, obligate brood parasitic icterid native to temperate and subtropical North America.

2484417.name: Bobolink
2484417.blurb: The bobolink (Dolichonyx oryzivorus) is a small New World blackbird and the only member of the genus Dolichonyx. An old name for this species is the "rice bird",

2484591.name: Golden-crowned Kinglet
2484591.blurb: The golden-crowned kinglet (Regulus satrapa) is a very small songbird in the family Regulidae that lives throughout much of North America.

2484605.name: Bohemian Waxwing
2484605.blurb: The Bohemian waxwing (Bombycilla garrulus) is a starling-sized passerine bird that breeds in the northern forests of the Palearctic and North America. It has mainly buff-grey plumage, black face markings and a pointed crest.

2484609.name: Cedar Waxwing
2484609.blurb: The cedar waxwing (Bombycilla cedrorum) is a member of the family Bombycillidae or waxwing family of passerine birds. It is a medium-sized bird that is mainly brown, gray, and yellow.

2484879.name: Red-breasted Nuthatch
2484879.blurb: The red-breasted nuthatch (Sitta canadensis) is a small songbird. The adult has blue-grey upperparts with cinnamon underparts, a white throat and face with a black stripe through the eyes, a straight grey bill and a black crown.

2484892.name: White-breasted Nuthatch
2484892.blurb: The white-breasted nuthatch (Sitta carolinensis) is a species of bird in the nuthatch family Sittidae. It is a medium-sized nuthatch, measuring approximately 15.5 cm (6.1 in) in length.

2487413.name: White-eyed Vireo
2487413.blurb: The white-eyed vireo (Vireo griseus) is a small songbird of the family Vireonidae.

2487430.name: Red-eyed Vireo
2487430.blurb: The red-eyed vireo (Vireo olivaceus) is a small American songbird. It is somewhat warbler-like but not closely related to the New World warblers (Parulidae).

2487441.name: Bell's Vireo
2487441.blurb: Bell's vireo (Vireo bellii) is a songbird that migrates between a breeding range in Western North America and a winter range in Central America. It is dull olive-gray above and whitish below.

2487446.name: Eastern Warbling Vireo
2487446.blurb: The warbling vireo (Vireo gilvus) is a small North American songbird. Its breeding habitat is open deciduous and mixed woods from Alaska to Mexico.

2487453.name: Yellow-throated Vireo
2487453.blurb: The yellow-throated vireo (Vireo flavifrons) is a small American songbird.

2487456.name: Blue-headed Vireo
2487456.blurb: The blue-headed vireo (Vireo solitarius) is a migratory songbird found in North and Central America. There are currently two recognized subspecies that belong to the blue-headed vireo.

2487596.name: Blue-gray Gnatcatcher
2487596.blurb: The blue-gray gnatcatcher (Polioptila caerulea) is a very small gnatcatcher native to North America.

2487805.name: Black-capped Chickadee
2487805.blurb: The black-capped chickadee (Poecile atricapillus) is a small, nonmigratory, North American passerine bird that lives in deciduous and mixed forests. It is a member of the Paridae family, also known as tits.

2487887.name: Tufted Titmouse
2487887.blurb: The tufted titmouse (Baeolophus bicolor) is a small songbird native to eastern North America. The species belongs to the tit and chickadee family (Paridae).

2488517.name: Scarlet Tanager
2488517.blurb: The scarlet tanager (Piranga olivacea) is a medium-sized American songbird. Until 2009, it was placed in the tanager family (Thraupidae),

2489129.name: Purple Martin
2489129.blurb: The purple martin (Progne subis) is a passerine bird in the swallow family Hirundinidae. It is the largest swallow in North America. Despite its name, the purple martin is not truly purple.

2489160.name: Bank Swallow
2489160.blurb: The sand martin (Riparia riparia), also known as the collared sand martin or common sand martin, and in the Americas as the bank swallow, is a migratory passerine bird in the swallow family Hirundinidae.

2489169.name: Cliff Swallow
2489169.blurb: The cliff swallow or American cliff swallow (Petrochelidon pyrrhonota) is a member of the passerine bird family Hirundinidae, the swallows and martins.

2489181.name: Tree Swallow
2489181.blurb: The tree swallow (Tachycineta bicolor) is a migratory bird of the family Hirundinidae. Found in the Americas, the tree swallow was first described in 1807 by French ornithologist Louis Vieillot as Hirundo bicolor.

2489202.name: Northern Rough-winged Swallow
2489202.blurb: The northern rough-winged swallow (Stelgidopteryx serripennis) is a small, migratory swallow. It is very similar to the southern rough-winged swallow, Stelgidopteryx ruficollis.

2489590.name: Ovenbird
2489590.blurb: The ovenbird (Seiurus aurocapilla) is a small songbird of the New World warbler family Parulidae. It is the only species placed in the genus Seiurus.

2489613.name: Black-and-white Warbler
2489613.blurb: The black-and-white warbler (Mniotilta varia) is a species of New World warbler, and the only member of its genus, Mniotilta.

2489670.name: Common Yellowthroat
2489670.blurb: The common yellowthroat (Geothlypis trichas) is a New World warbler. It is an abundant breeder in North America, ranging from southern Canada to central Mexico.

2489985.name: American Redstart
2489985.blurb: The American redstart (Setophaga ruticilla) is a New World warbler. It is only distantly related to the Old World (common) redstart, with both belonging to the order Passeriformes.

2489989.name: Yellow-breasted Chat
2489989.blurb: The yellow-breasted chat (Icteria virens) is a large songbird in its own family, Icteriidae, that is found in North and Central America.

2490263.name: American Pipit
2490263.blurb: The American pipit (Anthus rubescens), formerly known as the buff-bellied pipit, is a small songbird native to North America. It was first described by Marmaduke Tunstall in his 1771 Ornithologia Britannica.

2490327.name: Indigo Bunting
2490327.blurb: The indigo bunting (Passerina cyanea) is a small seed-eating bird in the cardinal family, Cardinalidae. It is migratory, ranging from southern Canada to northern Florida during the breeding season,

2490363.name: Dickcissel
2490363.blurb: The dickcissel (Spiza americana) is a small seed-eating migratory bird in the family Cardinalidae. It breeds on the prairie grasslands of the Midwestern United States and winters in Central America, northern Colombia,

2490384.name: Northern Cardinal
2490384.blurb: The northern cardinal (Cardinalis cardinalis), also commonly known as the common cardinal, red cardinal, or simply cardinal, is a bird in the genus Cardinalis.

2490494.name: Rose-breasted Grosbeak
2490494.blurb: The rose-breasted grosbeak (Pheucticus ludovicianus), colloquially called "cut-throat" due to its coloration, is a large, seed-eating grosbeak in the cardinal family (Cardinalidae). It is primarily a foliage gleaner.

2490810.name: Hermit Thrush
2490810.blurb: The hermit thrush (Catharus guttatus) is a medium-sized North American thrush.

2490821.name: Swainson's Thrush
2490821.blurb: Swainson's thrush (Catharus ustulatus), also called olive-backed thrush, russet-backed thrush, and salmonberry bird is a medium-sized thrush.

2490849.name: Townsend's Solitaire
2490849.blurb: Townsend's solitaire (Myadestes townsendi) is a medium-sized thrush, the only solitaire native to America north of Mexico.

2490872.name: Wood Thrush
2490872.blurb: The wood thrush (Hylocichla mustelina) is a North American passerine bird in the family Turdidae and is the only species placed in the genus Hylocichla.

2490926.name: Varied Thrush
2490926.blurb: The varied thrush (Ixoreus naevius) is a member of the thrush family, Turdidae. It is the only species in the monotypic genus Ixoreus.

2490935.name: Mountain Bluebird
2490935.blurb: The mountain bluebird (Sialia currucoides) is a migratory small thrush that is found in mountainous districts of western North America. It has a light underbelly and black eyes.

2490941.name: Eastern Bluebird
2490941.blurb: The eastern bluebird (Sialia sialis) is a small North American migratory thrush found in open woodlands, farmlands, and orchards.

2491081.name: LeConte's Sparrow
2491081.blurb: LeConte's sparrow (Ammospiza leconteii), also known as LeConte's bunting, is one of the smallest New World sparrow species in North America.

2491123.name: Grasshopper Sparrow
2491123.blurb: The grasshopper sparrow (Ammodramus savannarum) is a small New World sparrow. It belongs to the genus Ammodramus, which contains three species that inhabit grasslands and prairies.

2491205.name: Eastern Towhee

audio.by: No machine-readable author provided. Mdf assumed (based on copyright claims).

2491205.blurb: The eastern towhee (Pipilo erythrophthalmus), also known as chewink, joree, or joree bird, is a large New World sparrow.

2491651.name: Lark Sparrow
2491651.blurb: The lark sparrow (Chondestes grammacus) is a fairly large New World sparrow. It is the only member of the genus Chondestes.

2491678.name: Lapland Longspur
2491678.blurb: The Lapland longspur (Calcarius lapponicus), also known as the Lapland bunting, is a passerine bird in the longspur family Calcariidae.

2491684.name: Smith's Longspur
2491684.blurb: Smith's longspur (Calcarius pictus) is a bird from the family Calcariidae, which also contains the other species of longspurs.

2491719.name: Snow Bunting
2491719.blurb: The snow bunting (Plectrophenax nivalis) is a passerine bird in the family Calcariidae. It is an Arctic specialist, with a circumpolar Arctic breeding range throughout the northern hemisphere.

2491728.name: Vesper Sparrow
2491728.blurb: The vesper sparrow (Pooecetes gramineus) is a medium-sized New World sparrow. The only member of the genus Pooecetes, it is a pale sparrow with brown streaks that breeds across the grasslands of northern North America.

2491872.name: Fox Sparrow
2491872.blurb: The fox sparrow (Passerella iliaca) is a large New World sparrow. It is the only member of the genus Passerella, although some authors split the species into four (see below).

2492096.name: Field Sparrow
2492096.blurb: The field sparrow (Spizella pusilla) is a small New World sparrow in the family Passerellidae. It is about 140 mm (6 in) long and weighs about 12.5 g (0.4 oz).

2492109.name: Chipping Sparrow
2492109.blurb: The chipping sparrow (Spizella passerina) is a species of New World sparrow, a passerine bird in the family Passerellidae. It is widespread, fairly tame, and common across most of its North American range.

2492192.name: Lincoln's Sparrow
2492192.blurb: Lincoln's sparrow (Melospiza lincolnii) is a small sparrow native to North America. It is a less common passerine bird that often stays hidden under thick ground cover, but can be distinguished by its sweet, wrenlike song.

2492196.name: Song Sparrow
2492196.blurb: The song sparrow (Melospiza melodia) is a medium-sized New World sparrow. Among the native sparrows in North America, it is easily one of the most abundant, variable, and adaptable species.

2492235.name: Swamp Sparrow
2492235.blurb: The swamp sparrow (Melospiza georgiana) is a medium-sized New World sparrow related to the song sparrow.

2492870.name: Loggerhead Shrike
2492870.blurb: The loggerhead shrike (Lanius ludovicianus) is a passerine bird in the family Laniidae. It is the only member of the shrike family endemic to North America; the related northern shrike (L.

2493801.name: Carolina Wren
2493801.blurb: The Carolina wren (Thryothorus ludovicianus) is a species of wren common in the eastern United States, the extreme south of Ontario, Canada, the northeast and southeast of Mexico, and into northern Central America.

2493863.name: Marsh Wren
2493863.blurb: The marsh wren (Cistothorus palustris) is a small North American songbird of the wren family. It was formerly called the long-billed marsh wren to distinguish it from the sedge wren, then known as the short-billed marsh wren.

2493890.name: Grass Wren
2493890.blurb: The grass wren (Cistothorus platensis) is a species of passerine bird in the family Troglodytidae. It is widely distributed in central and southern America.

2494324.name: Evening Grosbeak
2494324.blurb: The evening grosbeak (Hesperiphona vespertina) is a passerine bird in the finch family Fringillidae found in North America. The evening grosbeak is bulky, with a large bill and short tail.

2494771.name: Pine Grosbeak
2494771.blurb: The pine grosbeak (Pinicola enucleator) is a large member of the true finch family, Fringillidae. It is the only species in the genus Pinicola.

2494936.name: Gray Catbird
2494936.blurb: The gray catbird (Dumetella carolinensis), also spelled grey catbird, is a medium-sized North American and Central American perching bird of the mimid family. It is the only member of the "catbird" genus Dumetella.

2495347.name: Mourning Dove

audio.by: Francis C, Ortega C, Cruz A

2495347.blurb: The mourning dove (Zenaida macroura) is a member of the dove family, Columbidae. The bird is also known as the American mourning dove, the rain dove, and colloquially as the turtle dove,

2495370.name: White-winged Dove
2495370.blurb: The white-winged dove (Zenaida asiatica) is a dove whose native range extends from the Southwestern United States through Mexico, Central America, and the Caribbean.

2495414.name: Rock Pigeon
2495414.blurb: The rock dove (Columba livia), also known as the common pigeon or rock pigeon (but see also Petrophassa), is a member of the bird family Columbidae (doves and pigeons).

2495696.name: Eurasian Collared-Dove
2495696.blurb: The Eurasian collared dove (Streptopelia decaocto), often called the collared dove, is a dove species. It is grey-buff to pinkish-grey, and has a black half-collar edged with white on its nape.

2496287.name: Yellow-billed Cuckoo
2496287.blurb: The yellow-billed cuckoo (Coccyzus americanus) is a member of the cuckoo family. Common folk names for this bird in the southern United States are rain crow and storm crow.

2497035.name: Common Nighthawk
2497035.blurb: The common nighthawk or bullbat (Chordeiles minor) is a medium-sized crepuscular or nocturnal bird of the Americas within the nightjar (Caprimulgidae) family, whose presence and identity are best revealed by its vocalization.

2497240.name: Burrowing Owl
2497240.blurb: The burrowing owl (Athene cunicularia) is a small, long-legged, primarily terrestrial—though not flightless—species of owl native to the open landscapes of North and South America.

2497295.name: Short-eared Owl
2497295.blurb: The short-eared owl (Asio flammeus) is a widespread grassland species in the family Strigidae. Owls belonging to genus Asio are known as the eared owls, as they have tufts of feathers resembling mammalian ears.

2497415.name: Eastern Screech-Owl
2497415.blurb: The eastern screech owl (Megascops asio) or eastern screech-owl is a stocky, short-tailed owl that is relatively common in Eastern North America, from Mexico to Canada.

2497541.name: Barred Owl
2497541.blurb: The barred owl (Strix varia), also known as the northern barred owl, striped owl or, more informally, hoot owl or eight-hooter owl, is a North American large species of owl.

2498017.name: Greater White-fronted Goose
2498017.blurb: The greater white-fronted goose (Anser albifrons) is a species of goose, closely related to the smaller lesser white-fronted goose (A. erythropus).

2498112.name: Northern Pintail
2498112.blurb: The pintail or northern pintail (Anas acuta) is a duck species with wide geographic distribution that breeds in the northern areas of Europe and across the Palearctic and North America.

2498155.name: American Wigeon
2498155.blurb: The American wigeon (Mareca americana), also known as the baldpate, is a species of dabbling duck found in North America.

2498161.name: Ross's Goose
2498161.blurb: Ross's goose (Anser rossii) is a white goose with black wingtips and a relatively short neck. It is the smallest of the three white geese that breed in North America.

2498167.name: Snow Goose
2498167.blurb: The snow goose (Anser caerulescens) is a species of goose native to North America. Both white and dark morphs exist, the latter often known as blue goose. Its name derives from the typically white plumage.

2498243.name: White-winged Scoter
2498243.blurb: The white-winged scoter (Melanitta deglandi) is a large sea duck. The genus name is derived from Ancient Greek melas "black" and netta "duck". The species name commemorates French ornithologist Côme-Damien Degland.

2498246.name: Surf Scoter
2498246.blurb: The surf scoter (Melanitta perspicillata) is a large sea duck native to North America. Adult males are almost entirely black with characteristic white patches on the forehead and the nape and adult females are slightly smaller…

2498250.name: Black Scoter
2498250.blurb: The black scoter or American scoter (Melanitta americana) is a large sea duck, 43 to 49 cm (17 to 19 in) in length. The genus name is derived from Ancient Greek melas "black" and netta "duck".

2498256.name: Canvasback
2498256.blurb: The canvasback (Aythya valisineria) is a species of diving duck, the largest found in North America.

2498257.name: Lesser Scaup
2498257.blurb: The lesser scaup (Aythya affinis) is a small North American diving duck that migrates south as far as Central America in winter. It is colloquially known as the little bluebill or broadbill because of its distinctive blue bill.

2498263.name: Redhead
2498263.blurb: The redhead (Aythya americana) is a medium-sized diving duck. Its scientific name is derived from Greek aithuia, an unidentified seabird mentioned by authors including Hesychius and Aristotle, and Latin americana, of America.

2498264.name: Ring-necked Duck
2498264.blurb: The ring-necked duck (Aythya collaris) is a diving duck from North America commonly found in freshwater ponds and lakes.

2498305.name: Ruddy Duck
2498305.blurb: The ruddy duck (Oxyura jamaicensis) is a species of duck, one of six extant species of stiff-tailed duck (genus Oxyura). In the 1940s, the ruddy duck was introduced to the United Kingdom, where it established a population.

2498326.name: Common Goldeneye
2498326.blurb: The common goldeneye or simply goldeneye (Bucephala clangula) is a medium-sized sea duck of the genus Bucephala, the goldeneyes. Its closest relative is the similar Barrow's goldeneye.

2498329.name: Bufflehead
2498329.blurb: The bufflehead (Bucephala albeola) is a small sea duck of the genus Bucephala, the goldeneyes. It breeds in Alaska and Canada and migrates in winter to southern North America.

2498338.name: Tundra Swan
2498338.blurb: The tundra swan (Cygnus columbianus) is a species of swan which breeds in the arctic, and overwinters in North America, Europe, and Asia.

2498343.name: Mute Swan
2498343.blurb: The mute swan (Cygnus olor) is a species of swan and a member of the family Anatidae within the waterfowl order. It is native to much of Europe and parts of Asia and (as a rare winter visitor) the far north of Africa.

2498345.name: Trumpeter Swan
2498345.blurb: The trumpeter swan (Cygnus buccinator), or simply the trumpeter, is a species of swan found in North America. The heaviest living bird native to North America, it is also the largest extant species of waterfowl,

2498375.name: Red-breasted Merganser
2498375.blurb: The red-breasted merganser (Mergus serrator) is a duck species that is native to much of the temperate to subarctic Northern Hemisphere.

2498387.name: Wood Duck
2498387.blurb: The wood duck or Carolina duck (Aix sponsa) is a partially migratory species of perching duck found in North America. The male is one of the most colorful North American waterfowls.

2498408.name: Hooded Merganser
2498408.blurb: The hooded merganser (Lophodytes cucullatus) is a species of fish-eating duck in the subfamily Anatinae. It is the only extant species in the genus Lophodytes.

4409023.name: Chimney Swift
4409023.blurb: The chimney swift (Chaetura pelagica) is a bird belonging to the swift family Apodidae. A member of the genus Chaetura, it is closely related to both Vaux's swift and Chapman's swift;

4848480.name: American Herring Gull
4848480.blurb: The American herring gull (Larus smithsonianus or Larus argentatus smithsonianus), also known as the Arctic herring gull or Smithsonian gull, is a large gull that breeds in North America,

5228514.name: Ruby-throated Hummingbird
5228514.blurb: The ruby-throated hummingbird (Archilochus colubris) is a species of hummingbird that generally spends the winter in Central America, Mexico, and Florida,

5228542.name: Broad-billed Hummingbird
5228542.blurb: The broad-billed hummingbird (Cynanthus latirostris) is a small hummingbird that resides in Mexico and the southwestern United States. Males and females have different features (see sexual dimorphism).

5228824.name: Pileated Woodpecker
5228824.blurb: The pileated woodpecker ( PY-lee-ay-tid, PIL-ee-; Dryocopus pileatus) is a large, crow-sized woodpecker with a prominent red crest, white neck stripe, and a mostly black body.

5229155.name: American White Pelican
5229155.blurb: The American white pelican (Pelecanus erythrorhynchos) is a large aquatic soaring bird from the order Pelecaniformes. It breeds in interior North America, moving south and to the coasts, as far as Costa Rica, in winter.

5229247.name: Forster's Tern
5229247.blurb: Forster's tern (Sterna forsteri) is a tern in the family Laridae. The genus name Sterna is derived from Old English "stearn", "tern", and forsteri commemorates the naturalist Johann Reinhold Forster.

5229400.name: Stilt Sandpiper
5229400.blurb: The stilt sandpiper (Calidris himantopus) is a small shorebird. The scientific name is from Ancient Greek; the genus name kalidris or skalidris is a term used by Aristotle for a gray-colored waterside bird.

5229487.name: Black-billed Magpie
5229487.blurb: The black-billed magpie (Pica hudsonia), also known as the American magpie, is a bird in the corvid family found in the western half of North America.

5229675.name: Western Kingbird
5229675.blurb: The western kingbird (Tyrannus verticalis) is a large tyrant flycatcher found throughout western North America, as far south as Mexico.

5229688.name: Eastern Kingbird
5229688.blurb: The eastern kingbird (Tyrannus tyrannus) is a large tyrant flycatcher native to the Americas. The bird is predominantly dark gray with white underbelly and pointed wings.

5229734.name: Eastern Wood-Pewee

audio.by: No machine-readable author provided. Mdf assumed (based on copyright claims).

5229734.blurb: The eastern wood pewee (Contopus virens) is a small tyrant flycatcher from North, Central and South America. This bird and the western wood pewee (C. sordidulus) were formerly considered a single species.

5229743.name: Olive-sided Flycatcher
5229743.blurb: The olive-sided flycatcher (Contopus cooperi) is a small to medium sized passerine bird in the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatcher family.

5229864.name: Bullock's Oriole
5229864.blurb: Bullock's oriole (Icterus bullockiorum, also known as Icterus bullockii) is a small New World blackbird. At one time, this species and the Baltimore oriole were considered to be a single species, the northern oriole.

5229935.name: Orchard Oriole
5229935.blurb: The orchard oriole (Icterus spurius) is the smallest species of icterid. The subspecies of the Caribbean coast of Mexico, I. s. fuertesi, is sometimes considered a separate species, the ochre oriole or Fuertes's oriole.

5230862.name: Blue Grosbeak
5230862.blurb: The blue grosbeak (Passerina caerulea) is a medium-sized North American passerine bird in the cardinal family Cardinalidae.

5231132.name: White-crowned Sparrow
5231132.blurb: The white-crowned sparrow (Zonotrichia leucophrys) is a species of passerine bird native to North America. A medium-sized member of the New World sparrow family,

5231139.name: Harris's Sparrow
5231139.blurb: Harris's sparrow (Zonotrichia querula) is a large sparrow. Their breeding habitat is the north part of central Canada (primarily the Northwest Territories and Nunavut, ranging slightly into northern Manitoba and Saskatchewan),

5231140.name: White-throated Sparrow
5231140.blurb: The white-throated sparrow (Zonotrichia albicollis) is a passerine bird of the New World sparrow family Passerellidae. It breeds in northern North America and winters in the southern United States.

5231142.name: Savannah Sparrow
5231142.blurb: The Savannah sparrow (Passerculus sandwichensis) is a small New World sparrow that is the only member of the genus Passerculus. It is a widespread and abundant species that occupies open grassland habitats in North America.

5231190.name: House Sparrow
5231190.blurb: The house sparrow (Passer domesticus) is a bird of the sparrow family Passeridae, found in most parts of the world. It is a small bird that has a typical length of 16 cm (6.3 in) and a mass of 24–39.5 g (0.85–1.39 oz).

5231198.name: Eurasian Tree Sparrow
5231198.blurb: The tree sparrow (Passer montanus Latin pronunciation: [pas.ser mon.ta.nus]) is a passerine bird in the sparrow family with a rich chestnut crown and nape and a black patch on each pure white cheek.

5231459.name: Northern House Wren
5231459.blurb: The northern house wren (Troglodytes aedon) is a very small passerine in the wren family Troglodytidae. It is found in southern Canada, the USA and Mexico. It occurs in most suburban areas in its range.

5231630.name: Redpoll
5231630.blurb: The redpoll (Acanthis flammea) is a species of small passerine bird in the finch family Fringillidae. It is the only species placed in the genus Acanthis. It breeds in the Arctic and north temperate Holarctic tundra and taiga.

5231635.name: Pine Siskin
5231635.blurb: The pine siskin (Spinus pinus) is a North American bird in the finch family. It is a migratory bird with an extremely sporadic winter range. The pine siskin is currently listed as a species of Least Concern on the IUCN Red List.

5231640.name: American Goldfinch
5231640.blurb: The American goldfinch (Spinus tristis) is a small North American bird in the finch family. It is migratory, ranging from mid-Alberta to North Carolina during the breeding season,

5232207.name: Northern Saw-whet Owl
5232207.blurb: The northern saw-whet owl (Aegolius acadicus) is a species of small owl in the family Strigidae. The species is native to North America. Saw-whet owls of the genus Aegolius are some of the smallest owl species in North America.

5232437.name: Canada Goose
5232437.blurb: The Canada goose (Branta canadensis) is a large species of goose with a black head and neck, white cheeks, white under its chin, and a brown body.

5232452.name: Cackling Goose
5232452.blurb: The cackling goose (Branta hutchinsii) is a species of goose found in North America and East Asia.

5846430.name: Franklin's Gull
5846430.blurb: Franklin's gull (Leucophaeus pipixcan) is a small (length 12.6–14.2 in, 32–36 cm) gull. The genus name Leucophaeus is from Ancient Greek leukos, "white", and phaios, "dusky".

5959118.name: Great Horned Owl
5959118.blurb: The great horned owl (Bubo virginianus), also known as the tiger owl (originally derived from early naturalists' description as the "winged tiger" or "tiger of the air") or the hoot owl, is a large owl native to the Americas.

5959143.name: Snowy Owl
5959143.blurb: The snowy owl (Bubo scandiacus), also known as the polar owl, the white owl and the Arctic owl, is a large, white owl of the true owl family.

6065818.name: Bonaparte's Gull
6065818.blurb: Bonaparte's gull (Chroicocephalus philadelphia) is a gull found mainly in northern North America. At 28 to 38 cm (11 to 15 in) in length, it is one of the smallest species of gull.

6092631.name: Black-throated Green Warbler
6092631.blurb: The black-throated green warbler (Setophaga virens) is a small songbird of the New World warbler family.

6092942.name: Chestnut-sided Warbler
6092942.blurb: The chestnut-sided warbler (Setophaga pensylvanica) is a New World warbler. They breed in eastern North America and in southern Canada westwards to the Canadian Prairies.

6093202.name: Bay-breasted Warbler
6093202.blurb: The bay-breasted warbler (Setophaga castanea) is a small species of songbird in the New World warbler family, Parulidae. It is one of 35 species in the diverse genus Setophaga.

6093209.name: Magnolia Warbler
6093209.blurb: The magnolia warbler (Setophaga magnolia) is a member of the wood warbler family Parulidae.

6093345.name: Northern Parula
6093345.blurb: The northern parula (Setophaga americana) is a small New World warbler. It is migratory and breeds in eastern North America from southern Canada to Florida.

6093350.name: Cerulean Warbler
6093350.blurb: The cerulean warbler (Setophaga cerulea) is a small songbird in the family Parulidae. It is a long-distance migrant, breeding in eastern North American hardwood forests and wintering on the Eastern slope of the Andes in South…

6093586.name: Kentucky Warbler
6093586.blurb: The Kentucky warbler (Geothlypis formosa) is a small species of New World warbler. It is a sluggish and heavy warbler with a short tail, preferring to spend most of its time on or near the ground, except when singing.

6093846.name: Blue-winged Warbler
6093846.blurb: The blue-winged warbler (Vermivora cyanoptera) is a fairly common migratory New World warbler, 11.5 cm (4.5 in) long and weighing 8.5 g (0.30 oz).

6093862.name: Louisiana Waterthrush
6093862.blurb: The Louisiana waterthrush (Parkesia motacilla) is a New World warbler, that breeds in eastern North America and winters in the West Indies and Central America.

7340170.name: Tundra Bean-Goose
7340170.blurb: The tundra bean goose (Anser serrirostris) is a goose that breeds in northern Siberia. This and the taiga bean goose are recognised as separate species by the American Ornithological Society and International Ornithologists'…

7340825.name: Winter Wren
7340825.blurb: The winter wren (Troglodytes hiemalis) is a very small North American bird and a member of the mainly New World wren family Troglodytidae.

7341606.name: Wilson's Warbler
7341606.blurb: Wilson's warbler (Cardellina pusilla) is a small New World warbler. It is greenish above and yellow below, with rounded wings and a long, slim tail.

7341800.name: Yellow-throated Warbler
7341800.blurb: The yellow-throated warbler (Setophaga dominica) is a small migratory songbird species in the New World warbler family (Parulidae) found in temperate North America.

7341805.name: Yellow-rumped Warbler
7341805.blurb: The yellow-rumped warbler (Setophaga coronata) is a North American bird species that can be commonly observed all across the continent. Its extensive range connects both the Pacific and Atlantic coasts of the U.S.

7341834.name: Mangrove Yellow Warbler
7341834.blurb: The mangrove warbler or mangrove yellow warbler (Setophaga petechia) is a New World warbler species. It a small bright yellow bird that is found in mangroves on the Atlantic and Pacific coasts of the tropical Americas.

7357320.name: American Tree Sparrow
7357320.blurb: The American tree sparrow (Spizelloides arborea), also known as the winter sparrow, is a medium-sized New World sparrow. It breeds in Alaska and Northern Canada and winters in Southern Canada and the Contiguous United States.

7415507.name: Tennessee Warbler
7415507.blurb: The Tennessee warbler (Leiothlypis peregrina) is a New World warbler that breeds in eastern North America and winters in southern Central America, the Caribbean, and northern South America.

7531611.name: Nashville Warbler
7531611.blurb: The Nashville warbler (Leiothlypis ruficapilla) is a small songbird in the New World warbler family, found in North and Central America.

7690702.name: Northern Shrike
7690702.blurb: The northern shrike (Lanius borealis) is a large songbird species in the shrike family (Laniidae) native to North America and Siberia.

7804446.name: Purple Finch
7804446.blurb: The purple finch (Haemorhous purpureus) is a bird in the finch family, Fringillidae. It breeds in the northern United States, southern Canada, and the west coast of North America.

8144830.name: White-winged Crossbill
8144830.blurb: The two-barred crossbill or white-winged crossbill (Loxia leucoptera) is a small passerine bird in the finch family Fringillidae. It breeds in the coniferous forests of North America and the Palearctic.

8169649.name: Orange-crowned Warbler
8169649.blurb: The orange-crowned warbler (Leiothlypis celata) is a small songbird of the New World warbler family.

8214667.name: Green-winged Teal
8214667.blurb: The Eurasian teal (Anas crecca), common teal, or Eurasian green-winged teal is a common and widespread duck that breeds in temperate Eurosiberia and migrates south in winter.

8323485.name: House Finch

audio.by: Francis C, Ortega C, Cruz A

8323485.blurb: The house finch (Haemorhous mexicanus) is a North American bird in the finch family. It is native to Mexico and southwestern United States, but has since been introduced to the eastern part of North America and Hawaiʻi;

8332393.name: Northern Shoveler
8332393.blurb: The northern shoveler (; Spatula clypeata), often known simply as the shoveler where other related species do not occur, is a common and widespread duck.

9149595.name: Downy Woodpecker
9149595.blurb: The downy woodpecker (Dryobates pubescens) is a species of woodpecker, the smallest in North America. Length ranges from 14 to 18 cm (5.5 to 7.1 in).

9192501.name: Hairy Woodpecker
9192501.blurb: The hairy woodpecker (Leuconotopicus villosus) is a medium-sized woodpecker that is found over a large area of North America. It is approximately 250 mm (9.8 in) in length with a 380 mm (15 in) wingspan.

9362027.name: Gadwall
9362027.blurb: The gadwall (Mareca strepera) is a common and widespread dabbling duck in the family Anatidae.

9362842.name: Dark-eyed Junco
9362842.blurb: The dark-eyed junco (Junco hyemalis) is a species of junco, a group of small, grayish New World sparrows. The species is common across much of temperate North America and in summer it ranges far into the Arctic.

9409198.name: Red-winged Blackbird
9409198.blurb: The red-winged blackbird (Agelaius phoeniceus) is a passerine bird of the family Icteridae found in most of North America and much of Central America.

9415596.name: Horned Lark
9415596.blurb: The horned lark or shore lark (Eremophila alpestris) is a species of lark in the family Alaudidae found across the northern hemisphere.

9422220.name: Blue-winged Teal
9422220.blurb: The blue-winged teal (Spatula discors) is a species of bird in the duck, goose, and swan family Anatidae. One of the smaller members of the dabbling duck group, it occurs in North America,

9479809.name: Brown Thrasher
9479809.blurb: The brown thrasher (Toxostoma rufum), sometimes erroneously called the brown thrush or fox-coloured thrush, is a bird in the family Mimidae, which also includes the New World catbirds and mockingbirds.

9480015.name: King Rail
9480015.blurb: The king rail (Rallus elegans) is a large, mostly brown rail native to North America, where it breeds in marshes.

9510564.name: American Robin
9510564.blurb: The American robin (Turdus migratorius) is a migratory bird of the true thrush genus and Turdidae, the wider thrush family.

9515886.name: Barn Swallow
9515886.blurb: The barn swallow (Hirundo rustica) is the most widespread species of swallow in the world, occurring on all continents, with vagrants reported even in Antarctica.

9537647.name: Common Merganser
9537647.blurb: The common merganser or goosander (Mergus merganser) is a large sea duck of rivers and lakes in forested areas of Europe, Asia, and North America. The common merganser eats mainly fish. It nests in holes in trees.

9539567.name: Green Heron
9539567.blurb: The green heron (Butorides virescens) is a small heron of North and Central America. Butorides is from Middle English butor "bittern" and Ancient Greek -oides, "resembling", and virescens is Latin for "greenish".

9581157.name: Brown Creeper
9581157.blurb: The brown creeper (Certhia americana), also known as the American treecreeper, is a small songbird, the only North American member of the treecreeper family Certhiidae.

9596413.name: Western Meadowlark

5228080.name: California Quail
5228080.blurb: The California quail (Callipepla californica), also known as the California valley quail or Valley quail, is a small ground-dwelling bird in the New World quail family, inhabiting western North America.

5228199.name: Eurasian Moorhen
5228199.blurb: The common moorhen (Gallinula chloropus), also known as the waterhen, is a bird species in the rail family (Rallidae). It is distributed across many parts of the Old World, across Africa, Europe, and Asia.

5228513.name: Black-chinned Hummingbird

audio.by: Francis C, Ortega C, Cruz A

5228513.blurb: The black-chinned hummingbird (Archilochus alexandri) is a hummingbird occupying a broad range of habitats from deserts to mountain forests and urban areas in the western United States, southern British Columbia, and Mexico.

5228612.name: Vaux's Swift
5228612.blurb: Vaux's swift (Chaetura vauxi) is a small swift native to North America, Central America, and northern South America. It was named for the American scientist William Sansom Vaux.

5229128.name: Black-necked Stilt
5229128.blurb: The black-necked stilt (Himantopus mexicanus), also called the pied stilt, is a locally abundant shorebird of North and South American wetlands and coastlines.

5229158.name: Brown Pelican
5229158.blurb: The brown pelican (Pelecanus occidentalis) is a bird of the pelican family, Pelecanidae, one of three species found in the Americas and one of two that feed by diving into water.

5229205.name: White Ibis
5229205.blurb: The American white ibis (Eudocimus albus) is a species of bird in the ibis family, Threskiornithidae. It is found from the southern half of the US East Coast (from southern New Jersey to Georgia),

5229389.name: Wilson's Phalarope
5229389.blurb: Wilson's phalarope (Phalaropus tricolor) is a small wader. This bird, the largest of the phalaropes, breeds in the prairies of North America in western Canada and the western United States.

5229498.name: Pinyon Jay
5229498.blurb: The pinyon jay (Gymnorhinus cyanocephalus) is a species of jay, and is the only member of the genus Gymnorhinus. Native to Western North America, the species ranges from central Oregon to northern Baja California,

5229681.name: Cassin's Kingbird
5229681.blurb: Cassin's kingbird (Tyrannus vociferans) is a large tyrant flycatcher native to western North America. The name of this bird commemorates the American ornithologist John Cassin.

5229684.name: Couch's Kingbird
5229684.blurb: Couch's kingbird (Tyrannus couchii) is a passerine tyrant flycatcher of the kingbird genus. It is found from southern Texas along the Gulf Coast to the Yucatán Peninsula in Mexico, Belize and northern Guatemala.

5229687.name: Scissor-tailed Flycatcher
5229687.blurb: The scissor-tailed flycatcher (Tyrannus forficatus), known as swallow-tailed flycatcher or scissorstail, is a long-tailed insectivorous bird of the genus Tyrannus, whose members are collectively referred to as kingbirds.

5229754.name: Western Wood-Pewee
5229754.blurb: The western wood pewee (Contopus sordidulus) is a small tyrant flycatcher.

5229882.name: Hooded Oriole
5229882.blurb: The hooded oriole (Icterus cucullatus) is a medium-sized New World oriole. The male of this species ranges in color from a bright orange to a paler yellow, with a black back, face, tail and bib,

5229893.name: Altamira Oriole
5229893.blurb: The Altamira oriole (Icterus gularis) is a New World oriole. The bird is widespread in subtropical lowlands of the Mexican Gulf Coast and northern Central America, the Pacific coast and inland.

5229903.name: Audubon's Oriole
5229903.blurb: Audubon's oriole (Icterus graduacauda), formerly known as the black-headed oriole, is a New World passerine inhabiting the forests and thickets of southeastern Texas and the Mexican coast.

5229930.name: Scott's Oriole
5229930.blurb: Scott's oriole (Icterus parisorum) is a species of bird in the family Icteridae, the oropendolas, New World orioles, and New World blackbirds. It is found in Mexico and the United States.

5230754.name: Violet-green Swallow
5230754.blurb: The violet-green swallow (Tachycineta thalassina) is a small North American passerine bird in the swallow family. These aerial insectivores are distributed along the west coast from Alaska to Mexico,

5230852.name: Painted Bunting
5230852.blurb: The painted bunting (Passerina ciris) is a species of bird in the cardinal family, Cardinalidae. It is native to North America.

5230861.name: Lazuli Bunting
5230861.blurb: The lazuli bunting (Passerina amoena) is a North American songbird named for the gemstone lapis lazuli.

5231138.name: Golden-crowned Sparrow
5231138.blurb: The golden-crowned sparrow (Zonotrichia atricapilla) is a large New World sparrow found in the western part of North America.

5231430.name: Canyon Wren
5231430.blurb: The canyon wren (Catherpes mexicanus) is a small North American songbird of the wren family Troglodytidae. A non-migratory species, these birds are found throughout western North America in dry, rocky environments such as cliffs,

5231474.name: Cactus Wren
5231474.blurb: The cactus wren (Campylorhynchus brunneicapillus) is a species of wren that is endemic to the deserts of the southwestern United States and northern and central Mexico.

5231483.name: Rock Wren
5231483.blurb: The rock wren (Salpinctes obsoletus) is a small songbird of the wren family native to the rocky areas of western North America. There are 8 subspecies of the rock wren, one of which is extinct.

5231643.name: Lawrence's Goldfinch
5231643.blurb: Lawrence's goldfinch (Spinus lawrencei) is a small songbird of erratic distribution that breeds in California and Baja California and winters in the southwestern United States and northern Mexico.

5231647.name: Lesser Goldfinch
5231647.blurb: The lesser goldfinch (Spinus psaltria) is a small finch in the genus Spinus native to the Americas. As is the case for most species in the genus Spinus, lesser goldfinch males have a black forehead, which females lack.

5231677.name: Northern Mockingbird
5231677.blurb: The northern mockingbird (Mimus polyglottos) is a mockingbird commonly found in North America, of the family Mimidae. The species is also found in some parts of the Caribbean, as well as on the Hawaiian Islands.

5231688.name: Curve-billed Thrasher
5231688.blurb: The curve-billed thrasher (Toxostoma curvirostre) is a medium-sized mimid native to most of Mexico and to the deserts of southwestern United States.

5231710.name: Long-billed Thrasher
5231710.blurb: The long-billed thrasher (Toxostoma longirostre) is a medium-sized resident songbird of South Texas and eastern Mexico.

5231713.name: California Thrasher

audio.by: Sasahara K, Cody M, Cohen D, Taylor C

5231713.blurb: The California thrasher (Toxostoma redivivum) is a large member of family Mimidae found primarily in chaparral habitat in California in the United States and Baja California in Mexico.

5232446.name: Brant
5232446.blurb: The brant or brent goose (Branta bernicla) is a small goose in the genus Branta. There are three subspecies, all of which winter along temperate-zone sea-coasts and breed on the high-Arctic tundra.

5789146.name: MacGillivray's Warbler
5789146.blurb: MacGillivray's warbler (Geothlypis tolmiei) is a species of bird in the family Parulidae, the New World warblers. It is found from southeastern Alaska and western Canada to Panama.

5789281.name: Royal Tern
5789281.blurb: The royal tern (Thalasseus maximus) is a tern in the family Laridae. The species is endemic to the Americas, though vagrants have been identified in Europe.

5789298.name: Willet
5789298.blurb: The willet (Tringa semipalmata) is a large shorebird in the family Scolopacidae. It is a relatively large and robust sandpiper and is the largest of the species called "shanks" in the genus Tringa.

5844900.name: Woodhouse's Scrub-Jay
5844900.blurb: Woodhouse's scrub jay (Aphelocoma[a] woodhouseii) is a species of scrub jay native to western North America, ranging from southeastern Oregon and southern Idaho to central Mexico.

6065844.name: Laughing Gull
6065844.blurb: The laughing gull (Leucophaeus atricilla) is a medium-sized gull of North and South America. Named from its laugh-like call, it is an opportunistic omnivore and scavenger.

6092637.name: Golden-cheeked Warbler
6092637.blurb: The golden-cheeked warbler (Setophaga chrysoparia) is an endangered species of bird that breeds in Central Texas, from Palo Pinto County southwestward along the eastern and southern edge of the Edwards Plateau to Kinney County.

6092644.name: Hermit Warbler
6092644.blurb: The hermit warbler (Setophaga occidentalis) is a small perching bird. It is a species of New World warbler or wood-warbler.

6092651.name: Townsend's Warbler
6092651.blurb: Townsend's warbler (Setophaga townsendi) is a small songbird of the New World warbler family.

6093199.name: Blackburnian Warbler
6093199.blurb: The Blackburnian warbler (Setophaga fusca) is a small New World warbler. They breed in eastern North America, from southern Canada, westwards to the southern Canadian Prairies, the Great Lakes region and New England,

6093357.name: Cape May Warbler
6093357.blurb: The Cape May warbler (Setophaga tigrina) is a species of New World warbler. It breeds in northern North America. Its breeding range spans all but the westernmost parts of southern Canada, the Great Lakes region, and New England.

6093374.name: Hooded Warbler
6093374.blurb: The hooded warbler (Setophaga citrina) is a New World warbler. It breeds in eastern North America across the eastern United States and into southernmost Canada (Ontario).

6093856.name: Northern Waterthrush
6093856.blurb: The northern waterthrush (Parkesia noveboracensis) is a species of ground-feeding migratory New World warbler of the genus Parkesia.

7340146.name: Sooty Grouse
7340146.blurb: The sooty grouse (Dendragapus fuliginosus) is a species of forest-dwelling grouse native to North America's Pacific Coast Ranges.

7341587.name: Abert's Towhee
7341587.blurb: Abert's towhee (Melozone aberti) is a bird of the family Passerellidae, native to a small range in southwestern North America, generally the lower Colorado River and Gila River watersheds, nearly endemic to Arizona,

7341600.name: California Towhee
7341600.blurb: The California towhee (Melozone crissalis) is a bird of the family Passerellidae, native to the coastal regions of western Oregon and California in the United States and Baja California and Baja California Sur in Mexico.

7341622.name: Canyon Towhee
7341622.blurb: The canyon towhee (Melozone fusca) is a bird of the family Passerellidae. Until 1989, the canyon towhee and the California towhee were considered to be a single species which was called the brown towhee.

7341770.name: Black-throated Gray Warbler
7341770.blurb: The black-throated gray warbler or black-throated grey warbler (Setophaga nigrescens) is a passerine bird of the New World warbler family Parulidae. It is 13 cm (5.1 in) long and has gray and white plumage with black markings.

7341776.name: Grace's Warbler
7341776.blurb: Grace's warbler (Setophaga graciae) is a small New World warbler that specializes in pine woods.

7341789.name: Prairie Warbler
7341789.blurb: The prairie warbler (Setophaga discolor) is a small songbird of the New World warbler family.

7341816.name: Pine Warbler
7341816.blurb: The pine warbler (Setophaga pinus) is a small songbird of the New World warbler family Parulidae. It is a permanent resident in the southeastern United States and also breeds in southeastern Canada and the northeastern United…

7341822.name: Palm Warbler
7341822.blurb: The palm warbler (Setophaga palmarum) is a small songbird in the New World warbler family.

7341828.name: Black-throated Blue Warbler
7341828.blurb: The black-throated blue warbler (Setophaga caerulescens) is a small passerine bird of the New World warbler family. Its breeding ranges are located in the interior of deciduous and mixed coniferous forests in eastern North…

7597244.name: Calliope Hummingbird
7597244.blurb: The calliope hummingbird ( kə-LY-ə-pee; Selasphorus calliope) is the smallest bird native to the United States and Canada.

8255548.name: Cassin's Finch
8255548.blurb: Cassin's finch (Haemorhous cassinii) is a bird in the finch family, Fringillidae. This species and the other "American rosefinches" are placed in the genus Haemorhous.

8293756.name: Lucy's Warbler
8293756.blurb: Lucy's warbler (Leiothlypis luciae) is a small New World warbler found in North America. This species ranges includes southwestern United States and northwestern Mexico. It is one of only two warblers to nest in cavities.

8959883.name: Ladder-backed Woodpecker
8959883.blurb: The ladder-backed woodpecker (Dryobates scalaris) is a North American woodpecker.

9088491.name: Nuttall's Woodpecker
9088491.blurb: Nuttall's woodpecker (Dryobates nuttallii) is a species of woodpecker named after naturalist Thomas Nuttall in 1843. They are found in oak woodlands of California and are similar to the ladder-backed woodpecker in both genetics…

9128444.name: White-headed Woodpecker
9128444.blurb: The white-headed woodpecker (Leuconotopicus albolarvatus) is a non-migratory woodpecker that resides in pine forests of the mountains of western North America.

9345027.name: Cinnamon Teal
9345027.blurb: The cinnamon teal (Spatula cyanoptera) is a species of duck found in western North and South America. It is a small dabbling duck, with bright reddish plumage on the male and duller brown plumage on the female.

9353154.name: Plumbeous Vireo
9353154.blurb: The plumbeous vireo (Vireo plumbeus) is a small North American songbird in the family Vireonidae, the vireos, greenlets, and shrike-babblers. It is found from the U. S. states of Montana and South Dakota south to Honduras.

9367409.name: Common Tern

audio.by: No machine-readable author provided. Mdf assumed (based on copyright claims).

9367409.blurb: The common tern (Sterna hirundo) is a seabird in the family Laridae. This bird has a circumpolar distribution, its four subspecies breeding in temperate and subarctic regions of Europe, Asia and North America.

9375033.name: White-faced Ibis
9375033.blurb: The white-faced ibis (Plegadis chihi) is a wading bird in the ibis family, Threskiornithidae. This species breeds colonially in marshes, usually nesting in bushes or low trees.

9406038.name: Red-naped Sapsucker
9406038.blurb: The red-naped sapsucker (Sphyrapicus nuchalis) is a medium-sized North American woodpecker. Long thought to be a subspecies of the yellow-bellied sapsucker, it is now known to be a distinct species.

9428437.name: Dusky Grouse
9428437.blurb: The dusky grouse (Dendragapus obscurus) is a species of forest-dwelling grouse native to the Rocky Mountains in North America.

9441907.name: Mexican Jay
9441907.blurb: The Mexican jay (Aphelocoma wollweberi) formerly known as the gray-breasted jay, is a New World jay native to the Sierra Madre Oriental, Sierra Madre Occidental,

9476062.name: Great-tailed Grackle
9476062.blurb: The great-tailed grackle or Mexican grackle (Quiscalus mexicanus) is a medium-sized, highly social passerine bird native to North and South America.

9533566.name: Pacific Wren
9533566.blurb: The Pacific wren (Troglodytes pacificus) is a very small North American bird and a member of the mainly New World wren family Troglodytidae.

9543753.name: American Three-toed Woodpecker
9543753.blurb: The American three-toed woodpecker (Picoides dorsalis) is a medium-sized woodpecker (family Picidae), which is native to North America.

9552291.name: Cassin's Vireo
9552291.blurb: Cassin's vireo (Vireo cassinii) is a small North American songbird, ranging from southern British Columbia in Canada through the western coastal states of the United States, including California, Oregon, and Washington.

9568685.name: Western Flycatcher
9568685.blurb: The western flycatcher (Empidonax difficilis) is a small insectivorous bird in the family Tyrannidae. It is native to western North America,

9568884.name: American Barn Owl
9568884.blurb: The American barn owl (Tyto furcata) is usually considered a subspecies group and together with the western barn owl group, the eastern barn owl group, and sometimes the Andaman masked owl, make up the barn owl,

9581438.name: American Black Duck
9581438.blurb: The American black duck (Anas rubripes) is a large dabbling duck in the family Anatidae. It was described by William Brewster in 1902.

9606873.name: American Dipper
9606873.blurb: The American dipper (Cinclus mexicanus), also known as a water ouzel, is a semiaquatic bird species native from North America.

9616953.name: Northern Pygmy-Owl
9616953.blurb: The mountain pygmy owl (Glaucidium gnoma), or northern pygmy owl, is a small species of owl from the family Strigidae. They reside throughout southern Arizona, New Mexico and Mexico.

9656686.name: Western Gull
9656686.blurb: The western gull (Larus occidentalis) is a large white-headed gull that lives on the west coast of North America and the Pacific Ocean. The western gull ranges from British Columbia, Canada, to Baja California, Mexico.

9709230.name: Spotted Towhee
9709230.blurb: The spotted towhee (Pipilo maculatus) is a large New World sparrow. The taxonomy of the towhees has been debated in recent decades, and until 1995 this bird and the eastern towhee were considered a single species,

9751099.name: Muscovy Duck
9751099.blurb: The Muscovy duck (Cairina moschata) is a species of duck native to the Americas, from the Lower Rio Grande Valley of Texas and Mexico south to Argentina and Uruguay.
